questions.question: The Purva Mimansa school of philosophy was founded by __________ in ancient India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaimini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Purva Mimansa school of philosophy** traces its origins back to Jaimini, who founded it in ancient India **around 400 B.C.**.
 
• **Jaimini** is renowned as the author of the Mimansa Sutra, a seminal text in Hindu philosophy.
 
• This school of thought, Purva Mimansa, places significant emphasis on the importance of yajnas (ritual sacrifices) and mantras (sacred utterances) in upholding the cosmic order.
 
• It asserts that human salvation can only be achieved by adhering to the principles laid down in the Vedas. Mimamsa is classified as one of the six orthodox schools of Indian philosophy, alongside Nyaya-vaisheshika systems.
 
• It underscores the significance of valid knowledge and holds that the Vedas are timeless repositories of all knowledge. According to Mimamsa philosophy, religion entails fulfilling the duties prescribed by the Vedas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Krishna Dvaipayana**, commonly known as Vyasa or Vedavyasa, is a revered sage in various Hindu traditions, prominently recognized as the author of the epic Mahābhārata.
 
• **Kapila, **also known as Cakradhanus, is another esteemed sage in Hindu lore. According to the Bhagavata Purana, he is the son of the sage Kardama and Devahuti, who was the daughter of Svayambhuva Manu and the sister of Mahasati Ansuya.
 
• **Patanjali, **alternatively referred to as Gonardiya or Gonikaputra, is renowned as a Hindu author, mystic, and philosopher. Although the exact timeframe of his life remains uncertain, estimates based on the analysis of his works suggest that he may have lived between the 2nd century BCE and the 4th century CE.

questions.question: Forest Research Institute, Dehradun was established as Imperial Forest Research Institute. In which year was it established as “Imperial Forest Research Institute”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1906**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Forest Research Institute (FRI) **in **Dehradun,** India, traces its **origins back to 1878** when it was established as the **Forest School of Dehradun**.
 
• Later, in **1906, **it was reconstituted as the** Imperial Forest Research Institute**.
 
• FRI serves as a premier natural resource service training institute for the Indian Forest Service and State Forest Service.
 
• Situated in a census town nestled between Kaulagarh and the Indian Military Academy, FRI is bordered by the Tons River to the west.
 
• The institute's main building, designed by C.G. Blomfield in 1929, is a significant national heritage site, featuring Greco-Roman architecture.
 
• Additionally, the institute offers wheelchair-accessible facilities, including entrances and parking lots.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dehradun**, situated in the Indian state of** Uttarakhand**, serves as its capital and is also its most populous city.
 
• It functions as the administrative hub of the Dehradun district and falls under the jurisdiction of the Dehradun Municipal Corporation.
 
• The city hosts the winter sessions of the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly, thereby serving as its winter capital.
 
• Nestled in the Garhwal region, Dehradun is home to the headquarters of its Divisional Commissioner.
 
• Recognized as one of the "Counter Magnets" of the National Capital Region (NCR), it is being developed to alleviate migration and population growth in the Delhi metropolitan area.
 
• Additionally, Dehradun aims to establish itself as a smart city in the Himalayan region.

questions.question: What is the strength of a hydrogen bond determined by?

options.text: Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the electronegative atom of one molecule and the hydrogen atom of another molecule
Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the electropositive atom of one molecule and the hydrogen atom of another molecule
Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the electronegative atom of one molecule and the oxygen atom of another molecule
Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the polar molecule and the hydrogen atom of another molecule

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the electronegative atom of one molecule and the hydrogen atom of another molecule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The strength of a hydrogen bond** is determined by the coulombic interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the** electronegative atom **of one molecule and the** hydrogen atom **of another molecule.
 
• These bonds can range from very weak, with energies of 1–2 kJ/mol, to extremely strong, exceeding 155 kJ/mol.
 
• A hydrogen bond arises from the attraction between a partially positively-charged hydrogen atom bonded to a highly electronegative atom, such as nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine.
 
• These bonds can form within different regions of a single molecule (intramolecular) or between molecules (intermolecular).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **An electronegative atom** is characterized by its tendency to attract electrons when participating in a chemical bond. This chemical property is commonly represented by the symbol X.
 
• On the periodic table, electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period and decreases from top to bottom down a group.
 
• The most electronegative elements are typically situated in the upper-right corner of the table, whereas the least electronegative elements are found in the lower-left corner.
 
• Fluorine ranks as the most electronegative element, while francium is considered one of the least electronegative. Additionally, oxygen and nitrogen are recognized as other examples of electronegative elements.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National human rights commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Human Rights Commission** is **NOT **a **constitutional body **in India.
 
• Established in 1993, the **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** is an autonomous statutory body mandated by the Protection of Human Rights Act of 1993, which was subsequently amended in 2006.
 
• Human rights are an integral component of society, and NHRC plays a pivotal role in safeguarding human rights in India.
 
• Serving as a vigilant guardian, NHRC oversees rights pertaining to life, dignity, liberty, and equality as outlined in Section 2(1) of the PHR Act.
 
• These rights, enshrined in the Constitution of India and upheld by international treaties, are enforceable by Indian courts. The establishment of NHRC aligns with the Paris Principles of Human Rights, 1991, which were adopted to promote and protect human rights.
 
• These principles, endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1993, serve as a guiding framework for NHRC's endeavours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Finance Commissions are periodically** constituted by the President of India under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution to delineate the financial interactions between the central government of India and the respective state governments.
 
• **The State Public Service Commission (SPSC)** is a constitutional entity responsible for administering examinations for state service appointments. Additionally, the SPSC offers guidance to the government on matters related to disciplinary actions and promotions.
 
• **The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)** is a constitutional body tasked with safeguarding the interests of scheduled castes in India.

questions.question: The Tomb of Razia Sultan in the state of Haryana is made of which building material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baked bricks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tomb of Razia Sultan** in the state of **Haryana **is made of** Baked bricks**.
 
• **Razia Sultan**, the daughter of Iltutmish, ascended the throne of the **Slave dynasty**, becoming the first woman ruler of Delhi.
 
• However, her reign faced opposition from the nobles, leading to her brother, Mohin-ud-Din Bahram Shah, assuming power. During this time, Razia married Negro Altunia, the Governor of Bhatinda. Together, they sought to reclaim the throne from Bahram.
 
• As they marched towards Delhi, Bahram dispatched his army to confront them. A decisive battle ensued near Kaithal, resulting in Razia's death on October 14, 1240 AD. She was buried at the site of her demise, with her original grave once located there.
 
• The current mausoleum, dating back to the late 16th century AD, stands as a testament to her memory. Constructed from baked bricks and lime mortar, the mausoleum is enclosed by a protective boundary wall.
 
• A closed arch adorns the western wall, while a small gate provides entry from the eastern side. Additionally, a mosque and a well were built nearby during the mausoleum's construction, adding to its significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Raziyyat-Ud-Dunya Wa Ud-Din**, commonly known as Razia Sultana, made history as the first female Muslim ruler of the Indian subcontinent and the sole female Muslim ruler of Delhi.
 
• Despite her remarkable ascent to power, her reign faced challenges from within the Sultanate.
 
• Following her dethronement by her half-brother and successor Muizuddin Bahram, Razia sought to reclaim her position by marrying one of the rebels, Ikhtiyaruddin Altunia.
 
• However, her efforts were met with defeat in October of that year, leading to her untimely demise.

questions.question: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Parliament **passed the **Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014,** which was subsequently approved by the President on **March 1, 2014**.
 
• This act, commonly referred to as the **Telangana Act,** came into effect on June 2, 2014, leading to the formation of two new states:** Telangana and the remaining part of Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• The enactment of this legislation was a response to the Telangana movement, which advocated for the creation of a separate state of Telangana.
 
• As a result, the state of Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated into Telangana and the residual Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, mandates the division of assets, liabilities, employees, and contracts between the two newly formed states, ensuring a smooth transition and administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In August 2013, the **Union Cabinet** established a **Group of Ministers (GoM)** committee to assess the feasibility of dividing Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The committee was chaired by the Union Home Minister, Sushil Kumar Shinde. Other members of the committee included the Finance Minister, P. Chidambaram, the Health Minister, Ghulam Nabi Azad, the Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister, Veerappa Moily, the Union Rural Development Minister, Jairam Ramesh, and the Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Narayanaswamy.
 
• The committee's objective was to examine various aspects of the potential division, drawing insights from the findings of the Srikrishna committee on Telangana.

questions.question: Which danseuse among the following was called to perform for Queen Elizabeth-II’s coronation festivities in 1953?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamala Lakshmi Narayanan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1953, **Kamala** was invited to perform at **Queen Elizabeth II's** coronation festivities. Kamala, also known as Kumari Kamala, is an Indian dancer and actress.
 
• She started her career as a child dancer and went on to appear in nearly 100 Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada films.
 
• In the 1970s, she transitioned into teaching the **Vazhuvoor style of dance,** specializing in this particular form.
 
• In 1970, the Government of India honored her with the Padma Bhushan, the country's third-highest civilian award.
 
• In 2010, she was bestowed with a National Heritage Fellowship from the National Endowment for the Arts in recognition of her significant contributions to the arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mrinalini Vikram Sarabhai,** renowned as an Indian classical dancer, choreographer, and instructor, founded and directed the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad. This esteemed institution offers training in various art forms such as dance, drama, music, and puppetry.
 
• **Sitara Devi,** an iconic figure in Indian classical dance, particularly Kathak, also excelled as a singer and actress. Her talent graced prestigious venues worldwide, including the Royal Albert Hall in London and the Carnegie Hall in New York, earning her numerous awards and accolades.
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale,** a theosophist, dancer, and Bharatanatyam choreographer was a trailblazer in Indian history. Not only was she a pioneer in promoting Bharatanatyam, but she also advocated for animal welfare. Rukmini Devi made history as the first woman to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Indian Parliament.

questions.question: Which disease is caused by excessive iron deposition within the reticuloendothelial cells of the liver, spleen and bone marrow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemosiderosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemosiderosis** is a **medical condition **characterized by the accumulation of **excessive iron** in the **reticuloendothelial cells of the liver, spleen, and bone marrow**.
 
• This condition is marked by the deposition of iron deposits known as hemosiderin in various tissues. Hemosiderosis is commonly associated with secondary hemochromatosis and is frequently observed in individuals reliant on transfusions.
 
• While it often presents with no noticeable symptoms, some individuals may experience manifestations such as hemoptysis, iron deficiency anemia, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, rapid breathing (tachypnea), difficulty breathing (dyspnea), paleness (pallor), rapid heart rate (tachycardia), bluish discoloration of the skin (cyanosis), crackling sounds in the lungs (crackles), wheezing, and fever.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paresthesia** refers to an abnormal sensation experienced on the skin, characterized by tingling, pricking, chilling, burning, or numbness, without any discernible physical cause. Typically painless, paresthesias can manifest anywhere on the body, although they most frequently occur in the arms and legs.
 
• Ariboflavinosis is a condition resulting from a deficiency in riboflavin, also known as vitamin B2. While relatively uncommon in developed nations, it can affect up to 50% of individuals in developing regions.
 
• **Dermatitis** is a prevalent condition marked by inflammation and irritation of the skin. It presents in various forms and has numerous causes, often leading to symptoms such as itchiness, dryness, or the development of a rash.

questions.question: Makaravilakku festival is celebrated in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Makaravilakku **is an annual festival celebrated on** Makara Sankranti in Kerala,** India, at the **Sabarimala shrine**.
 
• The festival is marked by the procession of the **Thiruvabharanam, **which consists of the sacred ornaments of Lord Ayyappan, and a gathering at the hill shrine of Sabarimala.
 
• Each year, approximately half a million devotees visit Sabarimala to witness this ritual.
 
• Makaravilakku has roots in a religious practice that was traditionally observed by the Malayaraya tribe, believed to be the descendants of Malayaman Kaari, in the Ponnambalamedu forest.
 
• This practice was later continued by The Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kerala, **situated on the** Malabar Coast of India**, was established on **1 November 1956,** as a result of the enactment of the States Reorganisation Act.
 
• It was formed by amalgamating the Malayalam-speaking regions of Cochin, Malabar, South Canara, and Travancore.
 
• Covering an area of 38,863 square kilometers (15,005 square miles), Kerala ranks as the 21st largest Indian state in terms of area. It shares borders with Karnataka to the north and northeast, Tamil Nadu to the east and south, and the Lakshadweep Sea to the west.
 
• With a population of 33 million inhabitants according to the 2011 census, Kerala ranks as the 13th-largest Indian state by population.
 
• The state is divided into 14 districts, with Thiruvananthapuram serving as the capital. Malayalam is the predominant language spoken in Kerala and serves as the official language of the state.

questions.question: Initially who among the following were subordinate to the Chalukyas of Karnataka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rashtrakutas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rashtrakutas** initially served as vassals to the** Chalukyas of Karnataka **before eventually establishing their own dynasty in the **Deccan region of South India**.
 
• **Dantidurga**, a subordinate chief of the Chalukyas, founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty. In the mid-eighth century, Dantidurga overthrew his Chalukya overlords and solidified his rule by performing the hiranya-garbha ritual, symbolizing his ascension to Kshatriya status.
 
• Despite not being born into a Kshatriya family, Dantidurga's ritual allowed him to claim legitimacy as a ruler.
 
• From around 755 to 975 CE, the Hindu Rashtrakuta dynasty governed over the Deccan and surrounding areas of India.
 
• They cemented their power through strategic alliances with neighboring kingdoms, utilizing matrimonial ties and political agreements to strengthen their position in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Satavahanas** were an ancient Indian dynasty that held sway from the mid-1st century BCE to the early 3rd century CE.
 
• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty governed extensive territories in Northern India from the mid-8th century to the 11th century CE.
 
• **The Pāla Empire** emerged as a dominant force in the post-classical era of the Indian subcontinent, with its origins in the Bengal region.

questions.question: The Principal of a Sanskrit College who represented a blend of Indian and Western culture was __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Principal of a Sanskrit College** who represented a blend of **Indian and Western culture** was** Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**.
 
• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was born to Thakurdas Bandyopadhyay and Bhagavati Devi.
 
• From a young age, he displayed remarkable intelligence and a strong passion for learning.
 
• He pursued his education at the Sanskrit College in Calcutta and successfully passed the law examination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy **was an Indian reformer and a founding member of the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which later evolved into the Brahmo Samaj, a significant social-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen** was a Hindu philosopher and social reformer who endeavored to blend Christian theology with Hindu philosophy.
 
• Debendranath Tagore, an Indian philosopher and religious reformer, played an active role in the Brahmo Samaj and became a member in 1842.

questions.question: Which of the following ritual dances is performed by the Kamar tribe of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tertali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kamar tribe of Madhya Pradesh** performs the **Tertali dance,** a ritual dance that blends various dance forms.
 
• Typically, two or three women partake in the dance, sitting on the ground and possibly wearing veils.
 
• They may also hold small swords in their teeth and carry ornamental pots on their heads.
 
• **Cymbals and Sirpa instruments** accompany the performance. Living in the forests, valleys, and hills of central India, the Kamar tribe primarily resides in the Raipur and Rewa districts of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• They are divided into endogamous clans, or gots, restricting marriage within the clan for cultural preservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ghapal, **a folk dance originating from Rajasthan, India, holds significance as a peripheral folk dance of the region.
 
• **Munari,** another folk dance, hails from the state of Odisha, India. Odisha boasts additional folk dances like Savari, Ghumara, and Painka.
 
• **Paika dance, **a martial folk dance, originates from the Chotanagpur plateau region, spanning across Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.

questions.question: Plants that are adapted to live under plenty of sunlight are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**heliophytes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plants** that are adapted to live under plenty of sunlight are called** heliophytes.**
 
• **Heliophytes **are indeed plants that are adapted to thrive in environments with plenty of sunlight.
 
• They are often found in open areas or at the top of a forest canopy where they can receive maximum sunlight exposure.
 
• **The banyan tree** is a great example of a heliophyte, with its sprawling canopy often dominating the upper layers of a forest.
 
• Heliophytes play an important role in the ecosystem by providing shade, habitat, and food for various organisms, as well as contributing to the overall biodiversity of their environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Xerophytes** are plants that have evolved to thrive in environments with minimal liquid water, often inhabiting dry habitats like deserts or snow-covered areas.
 
• **Neophytes **refer to plant species introduced into a geographical region in recent history and are not native to that area, while archaeophytes denote non-native plants that have become established in an area over an extended period.
 
• Protophytes, resembling primitive algae, encompass a range of organisms, including unicellular plants, bacteria, yeasts, slime molds, blue-green algae, and various simple green algae.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is NOT a tributary of the Indus river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Rind**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rind **is **NOT **a tributary of the **Indus River**.
 
• The Indus River is one of the major rivers in Asia, flowing through parts of China, India, and Pakistan. It has numerous tributaries that contribute to its flow.
 
• **The Zaskar River:** This river is indeed a tributary of the Indus. It originates in the Himalayas and flows through the Ladakh region of India before joining the Indus.
 
• **The Hunza River:** This river is also a tributary of the Indus. It originates in the Karakoram Range and flows through the Hunza Valley in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, before joining the Indus.
 
• **The Rind: **The Rind River is not a known tributary of the Indus. It doesn't appear in geographical references or maps as a significant river in the region.
 
• The Gilgit River: This river is indeed a tributary of the Indus. It originates in the Gilgit-Baltistan of Pakistan occupied region and flows through Gilgit before joining the Indus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Indus River, **originating from the** trans-Himalayan region,** is one of the **longest rivers** globally, stretching approximately 2,000 miles (3,200 km).
 
• Its drainage basin covers an expansive area of about 450,000 square miles (1,165,000 square km), with a significant portion, approximately 175,000 square miles (453,000 square km), nestled within the Himalayas, Hindu Kush, and Karakoram Range. The remaining area extends across the semiarid plains of Pakistan. 
 
• The Indus River receives its most significant tributaries from the eastern Punjab Plain, comprising the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej rivers.
 
• These rivers collectively lend their name, "Punjab" meaning "Five Rivers," to the region spanning both Pakistan and India.

questions.question: Which water reservoir has been declared a ‘Ramsar site’ on the list of wetlands of international importance in 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sur Sarovar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sur Sarovar, **also known as Keetham Lake, was designated as a **Ramsar site in 2020**.
 
• This man-made reservoir, located in **Agra, Uttar Pradesh,** was initially constructed to supply water to the city of Agra during the summer months.
 
• Sur Sarovar has transformed into a vital ecosystem boasting a diverse range of habitats, serving as a sanctuary for both migratory and resident bird species, in addition to hosting over 60 species of fish.
 
• A Ramsar site is a wetland area recognized for its international significance under the Ramsar Convention, an environmental treaty established in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, and named after the city.
 
• This convention facilitates global collaboration and encourages national efforts toward the conservation and sustainable utilization of wetland resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chilika Lake,** situated in the state of Odisha, India, is a vast brackish water lagoon, boasting the title of the largest of its kind in Asia and the second largest coastal lagoon globally, spanning an impressive area of 1,100 square kilometres.
 
• **Pong Dam Lake,** alternatively referred to as Maharana Pratap Sagar, stands as a substantial reservoir located in the Kangra district of Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• **Sarsai Nawar Jheel,** a permanent marsh, graces the landscape of the Etawah district in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Which of the following players is associated with billiards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pankaj Advani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pankaj Arjan Advani** is an Indian billiards and professional snooker player.
 
• Renowned for his exceptional talent, he has clinched the **International Billiards and Snooker Federation (IBSF) world championship** title a remarkable 27 times.
 
• Among his achievements are 18 billiards world titles, including 17 triumphs at the IBSF World Billiards Championship, along with one victory at the World Team Billiards Championship.
 
• In the realm of snooker, Advani has secured the IBSF World Snooker Championship thrice, in addition to two victories at the IBSF World Six-Red Championship.
 
• He has also claimed the titles of the IBSF World Team Cup and IBSF World Team Championship once each. Advani holds the record for the highest number of IBSF world championships.
 
• In acknowledgment of his remarkable accomplishments, Pankaj Advani has been honored with numerous awards by the Government of India.
 
• These accolades include the Arjuna Award bestowed upon him in 2004, the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna in 2006, the Padma Shri in 2009, and the prestigious Padma Bhushan in 2018.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Saurabh Chaudhary **is an Indian sport shooter who clinched the gold medal at the 2018 Asian Games in the 10m Air Pistol event.
 
• **Manika Batra** is an Indian table tennis player who holds the position as the leading female table tennis player in India. As of May 2023, she ranks 39th globally in the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF) rankings.
 
• **Sankalp Gupta** is recognized as a chess player.

questions.question: According to Human Development Index (HDI) report 2021-22, out of all the neighbouring countries of India, how many countries have got ranking in the ‘Very High Human Development’ category of HDI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **2021-2022 Human Development Index (HDI) report, four **of India's neighboring countries - **Sri Lanka, China, Bhutan, and Bangladesh **- are indeed ranked in the **"Very High Human Development" **category.
 
• According to the 2021-2022 Human Development Report (HDR) released on September 8, 2022, India was positioned at 132nd out of 191 countries.
 
• With an HDI value of 0.633, India's score falls below the global average of 0.732, placing it in the medium human development category. In the HDI 2021, India maintained its rank of 132.
 
• Myanmar held the 149th position, Pakistan was ranked 161st, Nepal stood at 143rd, and Sri Lanka secured the 73rd spot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The HDR for the year is titled **"Uncertain Times, Unsettled Lives: Shaping our Future in a Transforming World"**.
 
• This report builds upon and expands on the discussions presented in the 2019 and 2020 HDRs.
 
• The Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI) serves as a comprehensive indicator of essential aspects of human development.
 
• These dimensions encompass the attainment of a lengthy and healthy life, access to quality education, and the achievement of a satisfactory standard of living.

questions.question: 'Long Walk to Freedom’ is written by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nelson Mandela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Long Walk to Freedom" **is the autobiography of **Nelson Mandela, **South Africa's first democratically elected President, initially published in **1994 by Little Brown & Co**.
 
• The book chronicles Mandela's early life, upbringing, education, and his 27 years spent in prison.
 
• During the apartheid era, Mandela was labelled as a terrorist by the government and imprisoned on Robben Island due to his leadership role in the African National Congress (ANC) and its armed wing, the Umkhonto We Sizwe.
 
• The autobiography has been adapted into a film titled "Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom," directed by Justin Chadwick, written by William Nicholson, and produced by Anant Singh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela** was a prominent South African anti-apartheid activist and politician. He made history by becoming the first black head of state of South Africa, serving as President from 1994 to 1999.
 
• Mandela's presidency marked the culmination of a fully representative democratic election in the country.
 
• Throughout his tenure, Mandela's government prioritized the eradication of apartheid's legacy and worked towards fostering racial reconciliation.
 
• Mandela was an African nationalist and socialist, and he also held the position of President of the African National Congress (ANC) party from 1991 to 1997.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aung San Suu Kyi, **a Burmese politician, diplomat, author, and 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, served as State Counsellor of Myanmar (equivalent to a prime minister) and Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2016 to 2021.
 
• **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, **an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist, employed nonviolent resistance to lead India's successful campaign for independence from British rule.
 
• **Dalai Lama** is the revered title given by the Tibetan people to the foremost spiritual leader of the Gelug or "Yellow Hat" school of Tibetan Buddhism, which is the newest and most dominant of the four major schools of Tibetan Buddhism.

questions.question: As of January 2023, who among the following is the Chairman of Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC) of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manoj Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of January 2023, **Manoj Kumar** is the **Chairman of the Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC) of India.**
 
• Manoj Kumar, formerly an expert member of marketing at the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), has been appointed as the Chairman of this statutory body by the Government of India.
 
• This promotion comes as Vinai Kumar Saxena, the former Chairman of KVIC, assumes the position of Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
 
• With a background in marketing and rural development, Manoj Kumar previously served as an Expert Member (Marketing) at KVIC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** was established in April 1957 by the Government of India through the enactment of the 'Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act of 1956'.
 
• Operating as an apex organization under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, KVIC is responsible for overseeing khadi and village industries across India.
 
• Its primary objective is to plan, promote, facilitate, organize, and assist in the establishment and development of these industries in rural areas, coordinating with other relevant agencies in rural development efforts as needed.
 
• Initially, in April 1957, KVIC assumed the responsibilities of the former All India Khadi and Village Industries Board.
 
• While its headquarters are located in Mumbai, KVIC also operates six zonal offices situated in Delhi, Bhopal, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Mumbai, and Guwahati. Additionally, it maintains offices in 28 states to effectively implement its various programs and initiatives.

questions.question: The total female literacy in India as per the 2011 census was ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**65.46%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the 2011 census, India's female literacy rate stood at **65.46%**, while the overall literacy rate for the country was **recorded at 74.4%**, with **males having a literacy rate of **82.14 **%**.
 
• Over the years, there has been a significant increase in literacy rates nationwide, rising from 18.33% in 1951 to 65.38% in 2001. During this period, male literacy rates were higher at 75.85% compared to female literacy rates at 54.16%.
 
• Among the states in India, Kerala boasted the highest literacy rate in 2011, reaching 94%.
 
• Following Kerala were Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh, and the capital territory of Delhi, all with literacy rates above the national average. Interestingly, despite leading in literacy, all these states reported higher literacy rates among males than females.
 
• Additionally, the Jain community emerged as the most literate community in India, reflecting their significant emphasis on education and learning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The 2011 census of India,** also known as the 15th Indian census, was conducted in two phases: house listing and population enumeration.
 
• Commencing on April 1, 2010, the house listing phase focused on gathering information about all buildings.
 
• Additionally, this phase included the collection of data for the National Population Register (NPR), which aims to provide a 12-digit unique identification number to all registered Indian residents.
 
• This identification number will be issued by the Unique Identification Authority of India, utilizing the information collected during the house listing phase.

questions.question: What is the name of the evacuation operation conducted by the Government of India to evacuate the Indian citizens amidst the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Operation Ganga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Ganga** was a significant evacuation mission led by the Indian government to rescue its citizens stranded in neighbouring countries of **Ukraine during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.**
 
• The operation involved the transportation of Indian nationals from** Romania, Hungary, Poland, Moldova, and Slovakia back** to India, with assistance from these countries.
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi **held a crucial phone call with** Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy **on 26 February 2022, during which they discussed various issues, including the safety of Indian students in Ukraine.
 
• The first evacuation flight departed from Bucharest and arrived in New Delhi with 249 nationals at approximately 2:55 am Indian Standard Time (IST) on 27 February.
 
• Following this, four union ministers—Hardeep Singh Puri, Jyotiraditya Scindia, Kiren Rijiju, and V.K. Singh—were dispatched to neighbouring countries of Ukraine the next day to aid in coordinating efforts with local authorities and prioritize the evacuation process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operation Eagle Claw **was an ill-fated rescue attempt by the US military in 1980 aimed at freeing 52 embassy personnel held hostage in Tehran during the Iran hostage crisis.
 
• Executed on April 24–25, 1980, the operation was the culmination of five months of meticulous planning involving the Central Intelligence Agency and personnel from various branches of the armed forces.
 
• The mission underscored shortcomings in the US military's operational coordination and ultimately spurred the establishment of the United States Special Operations Command (SOCOM) in 1987.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of India was affected by the Kuka movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Originating in the districts of **Ludhiana and Amritsar in Punjab, India, in 1849, the Kuka movement, **also known as **Namdharis, **emerged as a religious and political response to the British political establishment of the time.
 
• Central to the movement was a desire to purify the **Sikh religion**, with followers known for their devout recitation of the guru's name.
 
• The Kuka movement played a notable role within the broader context of India's historic Non-cooperation Movement.
 
• Led by Baba Ram Singh, a revered religious figure, the movement made significant contributions to the country's struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kuka movement **appeared inevitable that a confrontation would arise between the Kukas and the British Government.
 
• This clash unfolded in 1871 and reached its peak during the Kuka raid on Malerkotla on **January 15, 1872**.
 
• The events of the Kuka outbreak of 1872 resulted in severe reprisals, marked by brutality rarely seen in our history. Many Kuka prisoners were tragically killed by cannons, while their leader, Baba Ram Singh, was exiled to Rangoon.
 
• In 1920, the Kukas initiated the publication of the newspaper 'Satyug', followed by the launch of the daily 'Kuka' in 1922. When Mahatma Gandhi initiated the Non-Cooperation Movement, the Kukas joined forces in solidarity.

questions.question: Shahid Parvez Khan, Budhaditya Mukherjee, Anushka Shankar and Hara Shankar Bhattacharya are well known players of which of the following instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shahid Parvez Khan and Budhaditya Mukherjee **are renowned players of the sitar, while **Anushka Shankar,** daughter of legendary sitar maestro Ravi Shankar, also plays the sitar. **Hara Shankar Bhattacharya** is a notable player of the sarod.
 
• Ustad Shahid Parvez Khan is a maestro of the Indian classical sitar, hailing from the Imdadkhani gharana, and is renowned as the primary exponent of the seventh generation of the Etawah Gharana.
 
• Pandit Budhaditya Mukherjee is a distinguished maestro of the Indian classical sitar and surbahar, belonging to the Imdadkhani gharana. His playing style is characterized by intricate vocalic playing and spectacular high-speed performance.
 
• Anushka Hemangini Shankar is a British-American sitar player and musician, known for her virtuosity on the sitar. She is also recognized as an occasional writer and actor.
 
• Pandit Harashankar Bhattacharya is widely acclaimed as an exceptional sitarist, revered for his mastery of the instrument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The sitar** is a plucked stringed instrument that originated in medieval India and belongs to the lute family.
 
• It is primarily used in Hindustani classical music and typically measures around 1.2 meters in length, featuring a deep pear-shaped body, a long neck, and 20 movable frets.
 
• To produce sound, the sitar is played by striking its main strings with a plectrum known as the mizrab.
 
• Its construction, sound, and playing technique differ significantly from those of a guitar. With more strings than an acoustic guitar, the sitar produces a richer sound, although chords are not typically played on this instrument.

questions.question: The High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on ______________by the Minister of Law and Justice, Kiren Rijiju.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**November 2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021 **was presented in the** Lok Sabha on November 30, 2021, by Mr Kiren Rijiju, the Minister of Law and Justice**.
 
• This Bill aims to modify the High Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1954, and the Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1958.
 
• These statutes govern the remuneration and terms of service for judges of the High Courts and the Supreme Court in India.
 
• According to these laws, retired judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, as well as their family members, are entitled to receive a pension or family pension.
 
• Additionally, they are eligible for an increased pension or family pension upon reaching a certain age, as per a specified scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The scale outlined in the **Bill comprises** five age brackets, starting from a minimum age of 80 and progressing to 100 years, with **increments at 85, 90, 95, and 100 years**.
 
• The additional quantum of pension or family pension increases proportionally with age, ranging from 20% to 100% of the pension or family pension amount.
 
• The Bill specifies that individuals become eligible for the additional pension or family pension from the first day of the month in which they reach the minimum age specified within the relevant age bracket.
